header: The trains that stop at Durgapur railway station (DGR), from RailRadar's station timetable (https://api.railradar.in/v1/stations/DGR/trains, an API that needs a key: the plant's own key, kept on the server only, in RAILRADAR_API_KEY). Each train has its number, name, kind, where it starts and ends, its arrival and departure at Durgapur, and the days it runs. It is the TIMETABLE, not live running status (the card says so). Here I read the answer, CHECK it and sort it; nothing is guessed:

* THE DAYS. RailRadar gives the days a train leaves its STARTING station; a train that starts far away reaches Durgapur on a later day ("arrivalDay": 2 means the day after it started). The days I show are therefore the days AT DURGAPUR: each day of the list moved on by (arrivalDay - 1). (checked against a third-party list on 13 Nov 2026: Jaynagar Weekly 13135 leaves Kolkata on Saturdays at 20:55 and is at Durgapur at 00:04 on Sundays.)

* THE DIRECTION. The answer does not say which way a train runs past Durgapur, only where it starts and ends. A train that ends at Howrah, Kolkata, Sealdah, Shalimar, Dankuni or Barddhaman runs TOWARDS HOWRAH; one that starts at any of them runs AWAY from it. A train with neither end among these is placed when one end is a station known to lie beyond Asansol (Patna, Barauni, Delhi...), or from its own route (the ROUTE_HEADING table below). Every other train goes in a third list ("other through trains") with where it starts and ends, rather than being given a direction the data does not support. "Towards Barddhaman" includes the few trains that go on from Durgapur to Suri and Malda instead of Howrah.
* THE KIND. "MEMU" is the local train; "Train on Demand" is a special (festival, Puja, Chhath); the rest are mail and express trains of every class.
A reply that is not the expected shape, or in which too many trains cannot be read, is an error, never a guess.

doc: THE DIRECTION OF THE TRAINS THE ENDS DO NOT SETTLE (neither end on the Howrah side or beyond Asansol): I read it once from each train's full route (RailRadar's /v1/trains/{number}: the order of the stops, Asansol before Durgapur = the train is moving towards Barddhaman, Asansol after it = moving towards Asansol), on 13 Nov 2026, one train of each pair. The other number of a pair runs the opposite way (checked: its two ends are the first one's reversed). I do NOT work it out from the train number: the odd = down, even = up custom depends on each zone's headquarters, and on this very list it fails for 14 of 238 trains (13417 and 15629 are odd and run towards Barddhaman). A train that is not in this table and whose ends do not settle it is shown in the "other through trains" list. The table is for the trains that run all the year; check it when the railway renumbers one.

behaviours: all 24 trains of the sample are read, for Durgapur
the local trains are the MEMU ones (7) and the express list holds the other 17

the days are moved on to the day AT Durgapur: 13135 leaves Kolkata on Saturdays and is at Durgapur at 00:04 on Sundays; 03008 starts on Tuesday and is here on Thursday (arrival day 3); a train that starts near is not moved
shiftDays wraps from the end of the week to the start and keeps the week in order
the chip says Daily, Mon–Fri, or lists the days, and its title spells them out
a train that ends at Howrah, Sealdah or Barddhaman runs towards Howrah; one that starts there runs away from it
a train that starts or ends at Durgapur itself is placed by its other end: Asansol to Durgapur runs towards Howrah, Durgapur to Asansol away from it

a train with neither end on the Howrah side is placed when one end is known to lie beyond Asansol (Puri to Patna, Chennai to Barauni: away from Howrah), or from its own route (Kamakhya to Bengaluru 12551 comes through Asansol and runs towards Barddhaman; its pair 12552 the other way)
the route table covers the pairs: the two numbers of a pair run opposite ways, and the odd number is NOT always the one going away from Howrah (13417 and 12551 are odd and run towards Barddhaman)
a train that is in neither the ends' rule nor the route table is not given a direction (a new special: 09999 from Chennai to Kamakhya), and the table never overrides a direction the ends give
headingOf never gives a direction to a train whose ends are both unknown, or both on the same side
a train that starts here shows only a departure, one that ends here only an arrival
the specials (RailRadar's 'Train on Demand') are marked as special; the Rajdhani, Shatabdi and Vande Bharat keep their class
every list is in the order of the clock at Durgapur (00:04 first, 23:53 last)
the next train of a list is the first one that is at Durgapur today, at or after now, among the trains that run today
on a Sunday at 07:00 the next train skips the Mon–Sat Shatabdi (12019 at 07:40) and takes one that runs on Sundays
nothing is next when no train of the list runs today after now
the filters: only the trains that run today, and without the specials
an answer that is not a success, or is for another station, or has no list, is refused
an answer with too few trains is refused (Durgapur has hundreds; 24 is below the default minimum of 50)
an answer in which more than a tenth of the trains cannot be read is refused; one bad train among many is skipped
a train with an impossible time, no days, or an arrival day of zero is not read (three bad trains among 96 are skipped)
the plant's RailRadar key is nowhere in the source (it lives in the environment only), and is never read under a name a browser can see
the key is read in one file only (the shared loader), in the server's environment
